chapter: Leaving music: Klessy and the Millers
title: The Miller family of musicians and Charlie Miller at the Frolic
summary: They sort out which Millers are related, and Charlie Miller's trombone with Sharkey at the Frolic in the early twenties.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well how does Johnny Miller fit in there...is he related to them at all?
And Eddie's not related at all...I don't know...different...families all together... So hard to keep them all straight...
Yeah...they got a...a group of Millers...they got Eddie... Eddie...uh...Eddie...the...the...the...the...tenor man...he's from here too... Uh-huh...and...is uh...is a...miller trombone player...
What's his name...his first name...and...I believe he played with Sharky...not too long ago...

Yeah...Charlie...Charlie Miller...yeah...and Philly...Philly and Teddy were brothers... Uh-huh...Charlie played a nice trombone...incidentally...he played with Sharky...years ago...back at the Frolic...
When did the Frolic open up anyhow?
Oh...Dick...around...that...that happened around...that must have been around the twenties...the early twenties...

Well I know Johnny Miller made those records...I don't know if you heard them or not... But Johnny Miller's New Orleans Frolicers...I think he was playing for the Frolic when he made the record... Maybe so...uh...

Old man had a...had a powerful nice band out there...Sharky was in his prime...yeah...he could blow that off that home...he played a sweet home... For my money...he still does...he still plays nice home...
